title: The geyser, a natural relaxation oscillator

data.source: Old Faithful eruptions 1-15 August 1985, Azzalini and Bowman (1990) Applied Statistics 39, 357-365; R package MASS dataset "geyser" via the Rdatasets collection (checks/data/ph-geyser.csv)

prediction: Memory reaches back further than one eruption: an age-weighted average of past eruption lengths (weight chosen on the first two thirds) forecasts the next wait at least 2 % better than the last eruption alone, on the final third.
baseline: The rangers' rule: next wait = a + b times the length of the last eruption only. Also the long-run mean and "same wait as last time".
why: The geyser does carry something over: a long eruption is followed by a long wait. But one eruption back is all the memory the data support. The averaged seed gave no real gain over the rangers' one-step rule, so CRR adds nothing here.
